paragraphs.text: Patients in hospital sleep badly: lights, alarms and night checks wake them again and again. One study found that the average patient was disturbed eleven times a night.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Several hospitals now group night checks together, so that a patient is woken once rather than three times. Staff also carry pagers that vibrate instead of ringing.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Sleep matters for recovery. Patients who sleep well leave hospital sooner on average, and confusion after operations is less common among them.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Not every ward can be quiet. In intensive care, monitors must sound, and nurses say that a completely dark room makes it harder to notice a change in a patient’s colour.
paragraphs.label: D

items.prompt: a benefit of good sleep for treatment
a reason why silence is not always possible
a measurement of how often sleep is interrupted
a change that reduces the number of times a patient is woken

groups.instruction: Questions 1–4. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A–D. NB You may use any letter more than once.
